public_rationale: The small increase in liquid assets is real, but the stated cause is not supported by the reconciliation. Approximately 95% is obtained by adding all investing and financing outflows. Those include $19.312 billion of share repurchases and $243 million of dividends. Net investing outflows alone consumed 52.5% of operating inflows, leaving $23.915 billion before financing activities. Calling the combined outflows circular financing materially misclassifies shareholder payments.
limitations: This conclusion uses the ordinary meaning of circular financing as funding customers or partners.
The small change in cash plus marketable debt securities is acknowledged; it is not equivalent to operating or free cash flow.
The exact customer-financing subset remains undisclosed, and later quarters are not used to judge the contemporary claim.
The decisive attribution is an evaluator calculation from company statements, not a company-reported circular-financing metric.

Circular financing means funding customers or partners that buy Nvidia products. It does not ordinarily include Nvidia repurchasing its own shares or paying dividends.
The quoted analysis supplies an approximate 95% absorption benchmark; near-zero means a small residual relative to operating cash inflow.
The target is the latest reported quarter available before the post: fiscal Q1 2027, January 26–April 26, 2026.

Because Marcus adopts an outside analyst's classification, the claimed attribution is treated as an estimate. Company cash-flow figures are inputs, not themselves a reported circular-financing measure.
The quoted $600 lacks a unit. It is treated as a rough contextual reference to millions, not as a separate exact-dollar claim.
